cohorts.subjects: Living people whose lumbar CT scans were taken from a hospital database (the CTs obtained from Carmel Hospital by the p. 2 ethics statement, from Assuta Hospital, Tel-Aviv, by the p. 12 one), Israel; Table 6 labels the population Israeli, no ethnicity given. Inclusion: examined in the hospital with no radiological findings and no complaint of back pain, without low back pain or DS, matched to the DS group by gender and age. Exclusion (all scans): slips other than at L4-L5, previous surgery, vertebral fractures, spondyloarthropathies, scoliosis, osteoporosis, transitional vertebra, isthmic spondylolisthesis. Retrospective; the 100 CTs were said to be randomly chosen from a database of 500 CTs of DS (p. 2).
cohorts.n_units: 50 lumbar CT scans, one per person; L1 to L5 measured (facet arthrosis graded T12-L1 to L5-S1)

cohorts.subjects: Living people with low back pain, lower-limb symptoms and single-level degenerative spondylolisthesis, grade 1-2, at L4-L5, from the same hospital CT database, Israel; diagnosis made separately by two senior spine surgeons of Assuta Medical Center on supine CT and standing radiographs. Same exclusions as the controls. The DS-vs-control rows are differences between this cohort and the control cohort.

techniques.instrument: K-Pacs Workstation Version 1.0.1 software; scanner, slice thickness and kernel not reported
techniques.how: Linear and angular measures on axial CT slices of L1 to L5 (Fig. 1 I-IV): the transverse facet angle between a midline line and each facet joint line, and the inter-facet angle between the two facet lines; facet width along each joint line, superior and inferior inter-facet widths between the joint lines' anterior and posterior ends; canal length (anteroposterior, posterior body wall to inner arch) and canal width (between the pedicles) on a slice through the pedicles; pedicle length and width on an axial slice; the Transverse Pedicle row of Table 5 is never defined. Landmarks are read from the figure's panels; the caption names only point pairs.
techniques.magnification: not applicable (CT, measured in mm by the software)
techniques.observers: one examiner (SA, the first author, 6 years' experience) took all measurements; intra-tester ICC(3,1) 0.85-1 on 10 CTs one week apart; inter-tester ICC(3,1) 0.85-0.92, second tester not described

techniques.how: On a parasagittal slice through the pedicles (Fig. 1 V): intervertebral foramen height from the lower edge of the upper pedicle to the upper edge of the lower pedicle (Table 4's columns L1 to L5 are the foramina L1-L2 to L5-S1, as Fig. 5 plots them), and pedicle height, the craniocaudal extent of the pedicle, left and right.

techniques.instrument: visual grading of the CT scans; plane not stated
techniques.how: Facet arthrosis graded 0-3 by Pathria's classification (0 normal, 1 narrowing, 2 narrowing plus sclerosis or hypertrophy, 3 severe osteoarthritis with narrowing, sclerosis and osteophytes), each side, joints T12-L1 to L5-S1, reported as the percentage of each group at each grade (Table 3).
techniques.observers: two examiners (first and second authors), blinded to diagnosis, grading all 100 scans by agreement, 6 months after the morphometry

within_paper: The control and DS cohorts are different people: 100 CTs split into a study group of 50 and a control group of 50 (p. 2, PDF 2). Both cohorts' scans were measured by both CT techniques and graded for facet arthrosis (all 100 scans, p. 3, PDF 3), so the tables share subjects across Tables 1 to 5. Table 6's Current study row is the control cohort (caption: in control groups; n 50; p. 12, PDF 12). Whether the 10 reliability CTs and the Fig. 1 example images come from the 100 is not stated (p. 3, PDF 3). The correlations of p. 7 pair this paper's measures with the same people's vertebral body and disc data published in [13].
